What a /32 means

A /32 is a single address. It is used for loopbacks, router IDs, host routes and ACL entries that match one host.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /32 uses 32 network bits and leaves 0 host bits, so the block contains 1 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−32) = 1; /31 and /32 are special cases.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Loopback0
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.255
!
access-list 10 permit host 192.168.1.1

Juniper Junos

set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/32

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.1/32 dev lo

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /32?

1. A /32 is one address.

What is the subnet mask for /32?

255.255.255.255. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.0.
